summary.text: A 2-year-old boy with Kagami-Ogata syndrome, confirmed by genetic analysis, was born vaginally at 31 weeks of gestation. Immediately after birth he developed severe respiratory distress requiring mechanical ventilation for 20 days and neonatal intensive care for 4 months, and needed oxygen up to 9 months of age. His respiratory condition then stabilized and remained stable before surgery.

He was scheduled for orchiopexy for bilateral cryptorchidism and had no previous surgery. Preoperative computed tomography showed marked tracheal deviation, at an angle of 90 degrees from the ventral to dorsal side. The M/W ratio of his small bell-shaped thorax was 67% at birth and 79% before the operation.

Plan A was a laryngeal mask airway after slow induction, with fiberoptic intubation as plan B. After oral midazolam premedication, anesthesia was induced by face mask with sevoflurane and nitrous oxide, rocuronium was given, and an LMA was inserted uneventfully. Caudal anesthesia with ropivacaine and sevoflurane maintenance followed; sugammadex was given at the end of surgery and the LMA was removed.
There were no adverse respiratory events and he was transferred to the general ward. His recovery was uneventful and he was discharged the next day.
